newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH RATE CUT SEEN LESS LIKELY AFTER GDP FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH RATE CUT SEEN LESS LIKELY AFTER GDP FIGURES.

text.p: Czech 1996 gross domestic product, which was reported to have risen by a higher than expected 4.4 percent, will make an interest rate cut less likely, anlaysts said.
"For the currency markets it means the crown may not weaken...it means the central bank is less likely to cut rates," said John Vax director of capital markets at ING Barings.

GDP slowed from 4.6 percent in the first quarter of 1996 to 3.6 percent in the third quarter after the central bank hiked the discount rate to 10.5 percent from 9.5 percent and minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent.

Kamil Janacek, chief economist at Komercni Banka said that the upturn in the final quarter of last year, when GDP rose 4.7 percent, was partly due to the weakness of the last quarter of 1995 - the base against which the new figure was calculated.
"The fourth quarter of 1995 was rather poor so also a statistical factor is playing some role," said Janacek.

Zdenek Tuma, chief economist at Patria Finance investment bank agreed that the figures were better than expected but said the markets would have to weigh up the relative importance of 1996 GDP against poor economic indicators released this year.

"There were bad figures at the beginning of the year so the question is whether the results for the whole of 1996 will be perceived as more important than the figures at the beginning of 1997," said Tuma.

Last week the statistical bureau said January industrial production declined by 3.9 percent year on year while construction output for the same period dropped 18.6 percent. -- Robin Shepherd, Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
